newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India ONGC's Bombay High Feb output down yr-on-yr.
newsitem.headline: India ONGC's Bombay High Feb output down yr-on-yr.

text.p: India's state-owned Oil and Natural Gas Corp Ltd's oil and gas production from its Bombay High basin in February fell year-on-year but its crude output will increase in April-May, a company official said on Tuesday.
February's crude output from Bombay High fell to 1.586 million tonnes, down from 1.714 million tonnes year-on-year, and from 1.644 million tonnes in January.
"In the long term, ONGC is still looking for a foreign consultant, but in the meantime it has taken action on its own at Neelam," the official said.
Neelam is one of ONGC's major fields at the offshore Bombay High basin, but production has been falling and is mainly responsible for the drop in crude production.
"There will be a marginal increase in production at Neelam in April or May," he said.
He said output at Neelam is expected to rise by around 100,000 tonnes per year, from its current production of 2 million tonnes per year.
Production from ONGC's remaining fields other than Bombay High, however rose marginally year-on-year to 43,000 tonnes from 42,300 tonnes.

Natural gas production from the Basin, ONGC's main gas producing area, fell in February to 1.0708 trillion cubic metres from 1.1479 trillion cubic metres in Februay last year. In January, 917.4 million cubic metres was produced.
"Gas is down because of the 22-day shutdown in January and February," the official said. "But it will be higher in March."
ONGC shut down some platforms in the South Basin of the Bombay High field to connect a pipeline to Hazira.

The gas pipeline which consists of two lines, each a 20 million-cubic-metres-per-day gas pipeline was completed seven months ago, but only the first line is being utilised with the second reserved for future upgrading.
February liquid petroleum gas (LPG) production, however, rose year-on-year to 89,770 tonnes from 87,370 tonnes, and from 83,450 tonnes in January.
